extraction.Name: Josephine Emery
extraction.Refused/Protested: We told the farmer I didn't want it but it came so I had to take it. The Farmer said we ought to have it, and he gave us application blanks but we never used them.
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: Mortgaged and sold. We sold the land and paid the mortgage.
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: Mortgaged only once to State of South Dakota, I guess it was for $1,000.00. No we sold the land and paid the mortgage. This was at the time of the war and we had to buy Liberty Bonds and we went in debt, and the taxes were so high.
extraction.Occupation/Income: We are staying with my son-in-law and my youngest boy.
extraction.NOTES: Did not sign a receipt for the patent; patent was sent to the bank near Bonesteel, kept about two years then sent to her; sold land for $17,000.00 cash; no dependents; not in good health; states 'If we hadn't received our patent, I believe we could have done better with our land.' Document header lists name as 'Mrs. Josephine Amery' but answers give name as 'Josephine Emery'; notary commission expires April 28, 1932; document dated 1929.
